THE LAUNCHER'S DRIVER-UPGRADE STEP (ADOPTED BY THE OWNER, 2026-11-11; lines marked RR in scripts/vm_run_rr.sh): another session's Lambda H100 hung on the VM's package lock in this step. The pinned step stops and disables apt's timers only (an apt-daily or apt-daily-upgrade service already running keeps the lock), runs apt-get over ssh with no wall-clock bound and the laptop's stdin (a dpkg conffile prompt would wait on it), and waits up to 600 s per install on the lock (two installs). RR's copy gives the WHOLE step ONE budget of 600 s: it waits for the package locks (no apt, apt-get, dpkg or unattended-upgrade process by name, no holder of dpkg's or apt's lock files; a VM without fuser reads as held, fail closed) naming the holder, and refuses when the budget is spent without killing anything; each install attempt (the pinned build, then the newest 580) runs as ONE command under `timeout --kill-after=30 <the budget left>` with stdin /dev/null, --force-confdef, --force-confold and NEEDRESTART_MODE=a, and starts with `dpkg --force-confdef --force-confold --configure -a`. THE BOUND KILLS DPKG: timeout signals the attempt's whole process group (apt-get and the dpkg under it, TERM then KILL 30 s later), which can leave packages half-configured. RECOVERY: the next attempt's dpkg --configure -a finishes that configuration before it installs; when the budget is spent, prepare refuses and the instance is terminated, never started or reused, so no session runs on a box whose install was killed. Tests run the step through stub apt-get, dpkg, pgrep, fuser, sudo and timeout tools: a process holding the lock, a lock-file holder, a non-matching process name, a lock never freed, no fuser, an interrupted dpkg left before the step, a hanging install killed with its process group (its child dead, dpkg left interrupted, prepare refusing), a prompt

readings.RR-R1 the counted miss fraction per cell: D = the median over the cell's counted calls of ncu's w1 dram__bytes_read.sum (cold L2 per launch, the session lock), READ with all 3 calls counted and their spread (max - min over the median) at most 0.03; C_u = each active expert's w1 once plus the unique tokens' A rows once (T x H x 2; design-P1 P1-F4); R = the re-read demand, sum over experts of (m_e - 1) x the expert's w1 bytes; m = (D - C_u) / R; counter sanity: D within [0.98 C_u, 1.05 (C_u + R)], else NOT READ. Printed beside: D / C_u - 1, w2's D against its compulsory bytes (each active expert's w2 once plus the intermediate rows once), ncu's w1 L2 read hit rate where proven, and the ncu clock (sm__cycles_elapsed.avg over gpu__time_duration.sum; ncu's clock under the 1410 lock read 1304 to 1350 MHz on B3's board, printed, never a refusal here)
